traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed technical requirements for 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT are concretely implemented and verified by tests.
• Core Functionality & Format (REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION): `@supports story-path REQ-ID...` is parsed and validated by the `valid-annotation-format` rule, with dedicated helpers in valid-implements-utils and comprehensive positive/negative tests.
• Deep Validation (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-SCOPED-IDS): The `valid-req-reference` rule parses @supports lines, resolves each story file, caches its requirements, and checks each REQ-ID against that file. Error messages include both the missing ID and story path, and fixtures confirm that the same requirement ID can exist in multiple story files without conflict.
• Backward Compatibility & Mixed Usage (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS): Existing @story/@req behavior is preserved (legacy tests still pass), and helper modules for story and req detection have been extended so that @supports counts as satisfying both story and requirement presence where appropriate. Tests for `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` explicitly verify that functions annotated only with @supports are considered valid, while unannotated functions remain errors. Mixed @story/@req/@supports usage is explicitly tested and accepted.
• Error Messages & Quality: Error messages for invalid @supports formatting and for missing requirements via @supports reuse consistent message patterns and always include the relevant story path, in line with earlier error-reporting stories. Rule implementations follow ESLint best practices (meta, schema, fixable, clear separation of helpers), and the feature is well covered by unit tests.
• Documentation: The migration guide and related docs clearly describe @supports, give examples of both annotation styles, and outline a gradual migration strategy, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the breadth of implementation and passing tests tied directly to this story file and its requirements, this specification is fully implemented.
